steps.name: Treated vs untreated composition test
caveats: Methods share underlying marker genes, so cross-method agreement is correlated evidence, not fully independent replication
Fractions are compositional: an increase in one cell type mechanically depresses the others, so directional claims must be read jointly and the uncharacterized/tumour fraction reported alongside
With 12 samples, an adjusted p-value near the threshold is weak evidence and should be presented as such
steps.context: Composition estimates here are the OUTCOME, not a covariate in a gene-level design — state this role explicitly. n=6 per group is small: only a large composition shift is detectable, and the analysis must say so rather than report a marginal adjusted p-value as a finding. The samples are unpaired biopsies from two different patient sets, so any difference is an association with treatment status, not a within-patient treatment effect.

grounding.reason: Scores compared between two groups: limma (or a rank test) on the score matrix under the design with BH across the tested sets per R-0134@0f16; the composition estimate is the outcome and its role is stated per R-0132@246d; a claim needs two or more concordant methods per R-0128@9eee

constraints: Use the actual condition labels from metadata.csv; the comparison is anti-PD-1 treated vs untreated
Do not pool p-values across methods and do not pick the method with the smallest p-value for a cell type
A composition claim requires agreement of two or more methods on the direction — single-method results are reported as non-robust
Report effect sizes and per-sample values, not p-values alone
steps.description: Test each cell type for a difference between the two conditions in metadata.csv, separately within each method's estimate table (EPIC, quanTIseq, MCP-counter, xCell, ConsensusTME) and for the UCell signature scores. With 6 vs 6 unpaired samples and one factor, fit limma on the score/fraction matrix under ~condition, or use a Wilcoxon rank-sum test where the distribution is clearly non-normal (fractions bounded at 0 with many zeros); state which was used per method. Then build the consensus table: a cell type is reported as a robust composition difference only when two or more independent methods agree on the direction of the change. BH adjustment applied across cell types within each method, stated explicitly
A consensus table marking which cell types show a concordant direction across two or more methods, and which do not
Per-sample dot/box plots for every cell type discussed, with sample_01 marked
An explicit written statement of statistical power at 6 vs 6 and of the unpaired, cross-sectional design limitation
An explicit statement that the composition estimates are the outcome of this test

plan.title: Melanoma TPM immune/stromal deconvolution: anti-PD-1 vs untreated
plan.analytical_narrative:
The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table (12,000 genes x 12 samples, salmon, human gene symbols) plus a 12-row metadata table with a single `condition` column (6 anti-PD-1 treated vs 6 untreated melanoma biopsies, unpaired, single batch). No raw counts and no quantification directories were kept, so every count-model route (DESeq2/edgeR size factors, tximport length correction) is unavailable by construction; TPM is the input scale and log2(TPM+1) is the only transform applied (R-0073). The research question is composition, not differential expression, so the plan is built around deconvolution with a signature-score cross-check and a per-cell-type between-group test.

T1S1 does sample-structure QC on log2(TPM+1): PCA/MDS on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and detected genes per sample. sample_01 was sequenced at ~a quarter of the median depth; per R-0008 it is kept, inspected, and reported rather than deleted — and because TPM is already depth-normalized within sample, low depth acts here through added sampling noise (fewer detected genes, compressed low-abundance estimates), which is precisely what the deconvolution steps must be checked against. T1S2 applies the 1 TPM in >=6 samples floor and produces the log matrix, but the deconvolution methods receive the UNFILTERED linear TPM matrix, because their reference profiles and signature gene sets expect the full gene space.

T3S2 is the primary composition estimate: EPIC and quanTIseq through the immunedeconv interface, both giving absolute fractions with an uncharacterized (tumour-cell) fraction from linear TPM. T3S3 adds MCP-counter, xCell and ConsensusTME as the cross-method layer, because no method ranks first for every cell type and a composition claim is only reported as robust when two or more methods agree on the direction (R-0128). ESTIMATE is not in this environment, so no tumour-purity number is claimed; the xCell immune and stroma scores stand in as relative measures and are labelled as such (R-0130). CIBERSORT/LM22 is likewise absent and is not substituted for (R-0131). T3S1 scores marker-based immune/stromal signatures per sample with UCell — rank-based, hence the least sensitive of the three families to sample_01's depth — as an orthogonal read on the same populations.

T4S1 does the actual between-group test: per cell type, treated vs untreated, on each method's estimates, with BH correction across cell types within each method, and effect sizes with confidence intervals reported beside the p-values. With n=6 per group this is underpowered for anything but a large composition shift, and the step is required to say so and to report the estimates per sample rather than only the group summary. T4S2 assembles the report with the reproducibility record. Note what this design cannot answer: the samples are unpaired biopsies from two groups, so a composition difference is an association with treatment status, not a within-patient treatment effect, and it is confounded with whatever else differs between the two patient sets.

quanTIseq, MCP-counter, xCell, ConsensusTME as cross-method consensus
UCell rank-based signature scores per sample with limma on the scores

Report the xCell ImmuneScore and StromaScore as RELATIVE stand-ins for the two ESTIMATE scores and label them as such — ESTIMATE is absent from this environment and no tumour-purity number is to be claimed. Build a per-cell-type concordance matrix (Spearman across the 12 samples) between the methods of this step and those of T3S2 for the cell types the methods share.
steps.context: immunedeconv 2.1.4, MCPcounter 1.2.0, xCell 1.1.0 and ConsensusTME 0.0.1.9000 are present. MCP-counter and xCell scores are between-sample abundance/enrichment measures, NOT proportions: they do not sum to 1 and a score of one cell type is not comparable with a score of another cell type. ConsensusTME requires the cancer type to be named — SKCM for melanoma biopsy.
acceptance_criteria: Per-sample score tables for MCP-counter, xCell and ConsensusTME covering all 12 samples
The ConsensusTME cancer type used (SKCM) stated explicitly
xCell ImmuneScore and StromaScore reported and explicitly labelled relative stand-ins for ESTIMATE, with no purity claim
A cross-method Spearman concordance matrix for shared cell types, spanning T3S2 and T3S3 methods
An explicit statement that MCP-counter and xCell outputs are scores, not fractions
constraints: MCP-counter takes log2(TPM+1); xCell and ConsensusTME take the expression matrix as immunedeconv expects for each — do not pass a log matrix where linear is required or vice versa
Never present an xCell or MCP-counter score as a cell proportion
Do not report a tumour purity value
State the cancer type passed to ConsensusTME
caveats: xCell spillover compensation reduces but does not eliminate signal bleed between related cell types (e.g. CD4 vs CD8 T cells)
xCell was trained on a full transcriptome; a 12000-gene matrix will leave some of its 64 signatures thinly covered — report coverage per cell type where obtainable

grounding.reason: Composition question spanning immune and stromal types: xCell for 64 enrichment-scored types per R-0126@a2be, ConsensusTME as the microenvironment consensus standing in for the absent ESTIMATE per R-0130@c0da, all through immunedeconv with a cross-method consensus per R-0128@9eee

steps.name: UCell marker-signature scores per sample
steps.question: What rank-based immune and stromal marker-signature score does each of the 12 biopsies carry, independent of any reference deconvolution model?
steps.description: Score each of the 12 samples with UCell on the filtered log2(TPM+1) matrix using immune and stromal cell-type marker sets (CD8 T, CD4 T, Treg, B, NK, monocyte/macrophage, dendritic, neutrophil, mast, endothelial, fibroblast) plus a small set of IO-relevant signatures (cytolytic activity, interferon-gamma response, checkpoint genes PDCD1/CD274/CTLA4/LAG3/HAVCR2). Marker sets must come from a curated human source — PanglaoDB or Human Protein Atlas tissue-elevated genes, or the scGate human TME / generic gating marker tables present in the reference store, whose master table carries semicolon-separated human gene symbols per population. For each signature, report its source, its version, and the number of member genes actually present in the matrix. UCell is rank-based per sample, so its scores do not depend on the other samples and are relatively robust to sample_01's depth.
steps.context: UCell 2.16.0 is present. The reference store holds scGate human TME and generic gating models (v0.17) with a master_table.tsv mapping population name to a semicolon-separated human marker signature — a usable curated marker source for this step; note that a trailing '-' marks a negative marker and such genes must be excluded from a UCell up-set. If neither a curated marker table nor the scGate tables can be resolved at run time, report that and fall back to hand-listed canonical markers with the gene list written out in full so the reader can audit it — this step enriches the composition picture but the deconvolution steps T3S2/T3S3 carry the research question.
acceptance_criteria: A UCell score per signature per sample for all 12 samples
For every signature: source, version, total gene count, and count of genes present in the 12000-gene matrix
Negative markers (trailing '-') excluded from up-sets if scGate tables are used, and that exclusion stated
An explicit statement that a marker-set score is a relative enrichment, not a cell fraction
The species (human) and the tissue of origin of the markers stated
constraints: input_scale = log_normalized_expression: use the filtered log2(TPM+1) matrix from T1S2
score_method = rank_based_per_sample
Do not present UCell scores as proportions or compare a score of one signature against a score of another
Write out every signature's gene list in the output so it can be audited
caveats: A marker of a cell type in one tissue is not necessarily a marker of that type in melanoma — state the tissue provenance
Signatures with few genes present in the reduced 12000-gene matrix give unstable scores and must be flagged rather than reported at face value

grounding.reason: Per-sample cell-type signature scores with no reference profile: UCell rank-based scoring per R-0133@ce76, marker sets from PanglaoDB/HPA-class curated sources with species, tissue and genes-present stated per R-0135@f02d

steps.name: Treated vs untreated composition test
steps.question: For each immune and stromal cell type, does its estimated abundance differ between the 6 anti-PD-1 treated and the 6 untreated melanoma biopsies, and do two or more methods agree on the direction?
steps.description: Test each cell type for a difference between the two conditions in metadata.csv, separately within each method's estimate table (EPIC, quanTIseq, MCP-counter, xCell, ConsensusTME) and for the UCell signature scores. With 6 vs 6 unpaired samples and one factor, fit limma on the score/fraction matrix under ~condition, or use a Wilcoxon rank-sum test where the distribution is clearly non-normal (fractions bounded at 0 with many zeros); state which was used per method. Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg ACROSS CELL TYPES WITHIN EACH METHOD, and report the number of tests. Report per cell type: both group means/medians, the effect size with a confidence interval, the raw and adjusted p-value, and the direction. Then build the consensus table: a cell type is reported as a robust composition difference only when two or more independent methods agree on the direction of the change. Plot per-sample values (not just group summaries) for every cell type discussed, with sample_01 marked.
steps.context: Composition estimates here are the OUTCOME, not a covariate in a gene-level design — state this role explicitly. n=6 per group is small: only a large composition shift is detectable, and the analysis must say so rather than report a marginal adjusted p-value as a finding. The samples are unpaired biopsies from two different patient sets, so any difference is an association with treatment status, not a within-patient treatment effect.
acceptance_criteria: A per-cell-type, per-method test table with group summaries, effect size + CI, raw p, BH-adjusted p, and n tests
BH adjustment applied across cell types within each method, stated explicitly
A consensus table marking which cell types show a concordant direction across two or more methods, and which do not
Per-sample dot/box plots for every cell type discussed, with sample_01 marked
An explicit written statement of statistical power at 6 vs 6 and of the unpaired, cross-sectional design limitation
An explicit statement that the composition estimates are the outcome of this test
constraints: Use the actual condition labels from metadata.csv; the comparison is anti-PD-1 treated vs untreated
Do not pool p-values across methods and do not pick the method with the smallest p-value for a cell type
A composition claim requires agreement of two or more methods on the direction — single-method results are reported as non-robust
Report effect sizes and per-sample values, not p-values alone
caveats: Methods share underlying marker genes, so cross-method agreement is correlated evidence, not fully independent replication
Fractions are compositional: an increase in one cell type mechanically depresses the others, so directional claims must be read jointly and the uncharacterized/tumour fraction reported alongside
With 12 samples, an adjusted p-value near the threshold is weak evidence and should be presented as such

grounding.reason: Scores compared between two groups: limma (or a rank test) on the score matrix under the design with BH across the tested sets per R-0134@0f16; the composition estimate is the outcome and its role is stated per R-0132@246d; a claim needs two or more concordant methods per R-0128@9eee

steps.name: Composition report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the immune and stromal composition of each of the 12 melanoma biopsies, and which differences between anti-PD-1 treated and untreated samples are supported by more than one method?
steps.description: Assemble the final report: a per-sample composition table and stacked barplot (EPIC and quanTIseq absolute fractions including the uncharacterized fraction), the score heatmaps for MCP-counter, xCell, ConsensusTME and UCell, the cross-method concordance matrix, and the consensus differential-composition table from T4S1. Lead with what each sample's composition is (the first half of the research question) before the group comparison. State the constraints that shaped this analysis: TPM only (no counts, so no count-model route), 12000-gene reduced matrix, ESTIMATE and CIBERSORT absent, sample_01 at ~a quarter of median depth, n=6 per group and unpaired. Close with a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, any random seed used, and the version of every marker collection and reference signature consumed.
steps.context: This is the deliverable that answers the research question. The composition-per-sample answer is well supported; the between-group answer is underpowered and must be presented with that qualification rather than as a result.
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample composition table and figure covering all 12 samples, with the uncharacterized fraction shown
A consensus differential-composition table showing which cell types agree across methods and which do not
An explicit limitations section naming: TPM-only input, 12000-gene matrix, absent ESTIMATE/CIBERSORT, sample_01 depth, n=6 unpaired
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seeds, and marker/reference collection versions
No tumour-purity value and no LM22-labelled result anywhere in the report
constraints: Answer the per-sample composition question explicitly and first; the group difference is secondary
Do not present an underpowered or single-method group difference as an established finding
Record the seed for any step using randomness
caveats: Cross-sectional treated-vs-untreated biopsies cannot separate a treatment effect from baseline differences between the two patient sets

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step itself; the reproducibility record follows R-0086@becf

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

EPIC absolute cell fractions from TPM with uncharacterized fraction
quanTIseq, MCP-counter, xCell, ConsensusTME as cross-method consensus
